audit.whatIsWrong: Every row of the level chart reads 'Skill' in both layers, while the prose says level 1 is hers ('she pokes you for free') and two items is hers ('she outscales your squishy, short-range DPS'). The chart and the text contradict each other.
audit.why: Mel out-ranges Cassiopeia at every stage - Radiant Volley 950 and Solar Snare 1000 against Noxious Blast 850 and Twin Fang 700 - so level 1 belongs to her; Cassiopeia's window is levels 3-6 when the Q-into-Twin-Fang refund loop peaks. The packet levelChart agrees: [Mel, Skill, Skill, Cassiopeia, Cassiopeia, Skill, Mel].
audit.corrected: NOT WRITTEN - flipping a side string ('Skill' to 'Mel') is a 5-to-3 character change and fails the +/-10% band in both layers. Recorded here and in questionsForUser.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rebuttal is named as the matchup-defining cooldown in four places with no duration attached anywhere.
audit.why: Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26s. At 38 seconds in lane it is not a per-trade button but a once-a-wave gate, which is what makes 'bait it first' a real plan rather than a slogan. The already-audited Mel side found the generator table carrying 20s for it, which is wrong at every rank.
audit.corrected: 38s now appears in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, spikes[3].text and whys[6].

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fields call Rebuttal her R - 'her R reduces/reflects your incoming damage', 'bait the R out before you commit', 'dumping your burst into her R'. Rebuttal is her W; her R is Golden Eclipse. Separately, nothing said which of Cassiopeia's abilities the reflect can actually catch.
audit.why: Riot's kit: W Rebuttal forms a barrier that reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker and prevents her taking damage; R Golden Eclipse strikes all enemies marked with Overwhelm regardless of distance. On Cassiopeia's side only Twin Fang carries a projectile flag - Noxious Blast is a delayed ground zone and Petrifying Gaze is a cone - so Rebuttal can only ever reflect Twin Fang. That makes the rule sharp: poke through Rebuttal with Q, never with E.
audit.corrected: All three now say Rebuttal (W) and state that Twin Fang is the only thing it can reflect while Noxious Blast passes it untouched.

audit.why: content early already states plainly that Miasma's grounding and Mel's lack of a dash cancel out - the one matchup in this slice where the grounding is genuinely dead. The already-audited Mel side reached the same conclusion. Left as written; the slow still holds her inside Twin Fang's 700.

audit.whatIsWrong: CHAMP_FULL tldr for this matchup is verbatim Lucian boilerplate - 'He pokes in bursts, you poke forever' - with male pronouns for Mel and a treadmill claim that is the opposite of true here. dosFull[1].d and tradeBad are the same Lucian paste, referencing a 'grounded zone's edge' that does nothing to Mel.
audit.why: Mel out-ranges Cassiopeia, so the treadmill never gets to run, and Mel has no dash for the grounded zone to catch.
audit.corrected: tldr, dosFull[1].d and tradeBad rewritten to the actual matchup.

edits.before: This is your window. With ranks in Q and E you fire a Twin Fang off every Q or W poison tick, refunding most of its cooldown, and your boots-free passive speed plus Q's on-hit burst let you stick to her once you commit — her single-cast poke can't out-damage your ramping per-hit DPS in a sustained trade. At 6, Petrifying Gaze answers her range: turn into her so the cone stun lands, then E-spam through her while she's locked. The trap to avoid is dumping your burst into her R — Rebuttal reduces and reflects incoming damage, so a Twin Fang chain into an active R is wasted (and a reflected projectile chunks you), so make her use it first.

edits.before: She reclaims the lane at 2+ items. Get your kills in the level-3-to-6 window where your refunded Twin Fang DPS spikes hardest; if you let her free-farm to two items she just zones you with Q range and never has to step into your poison. Side-step her Q, ward for ganks, and make the mid-game count before her scaling pulls ahead of yours.
